service.description: The in-parameters the People app services share; each service declares what it returns.

Check that the user may open People and resolve their scope and the app's routes: capabilities (the People and payroll permissions, and the areas), the employers a staff reader sees as options and whether they are every one, the units under them, the user's own party and current employments, and the links. A self-service employee without People (P8: their own grant on the self-service screen) gets a context of their own: the capability self, their own party and employments, and the self-service link. Refuses a user without People (PEOPLE_UNAVAILABLE), a Projects client contact and a PASS public account among them, and another app root (PEOPLE_CONTEXT). Pay values are never part of it.

parameter.name: defaultOrganizationPartyId
parameter.description: A new record's organization when none is chosen: the active one, the only one, or the user's own (FacilityScope.js defaultOrganization)

parameter.name: organizationOptions
parameter.description: The employers as {value, label}, by name, at most 100

service.description: A record a People screen or mount was given: an employer or a person (People.js recordKinds; later phases add theirs). Answers its kind's name, a label and a short detail (a person's employers in the user's scope). Refuses a record that does not exist and one outside the scope alike (RECORD_UNAVAILABLE): an organization that is not an employer the user sees, a person neither self, a live report nor employed by such an employer. With a capability named (hrView, configure, ...), refuses a user without it (PERMISSION_DENIED).

parameter.name: recordType
parameter.description: organization or person

service.description: The options of a People drop-down the user may choose, searched by term in the query ignoring case, with the selected value's label: employers (those a staff reader sees), units (the employers and the departments and teams under them), people (the current employees of those employers, the user's live reports and the user with self-service), employees (P3: the current employees of organizationPartyId, else of every employer the user reads, the managers and members OrgStructure and OrgChart choose), departments (P4: the departments of organizationPartyId, a position's), jobClasses (the current job classes), payGrades (the pay grades by name, never an amount), staff (P5: organizationPartyId's employees and agents), positions (P6: organizationPartyId's seats in effect and not inactive, vacant ones first, narrowed to departmentPartyId), workLocations (P6: organizationPartyId's facilities) and terminationReasons and terminationTypes (P6: People's lookups, ended values left out), leaveTypes and leavePolicies (P11: People's leave types; an HR reader's policies not closed, of organizationPartyId when given); skillTypes, skillLevels and qualificationTypes (P18: People's lookups, ended values left out; a level by its number); trainers (P19: the employees and agents of a development reader's employers) and trainingForms (P19: the published training assessment forms of organizationPartyId, else of every employer the user reads); payComponents, payGroups and glAccounts (P22: a payroll reader's, of organizationPartyId: its pay components in use by code and name, its pay groups, its accounts by code and name; never an amount) and payrollLocalizations (P22: the registered localizations); payEmployments, payStructures, payElections and benefitTypes (P23: a payroll reader's: organizationPartyId's current employments by the person's name, its structures published and not ended, the elective lines of payrollStructureId, and the benefit types; never an amount); hoursGroups, payPeriods and payAdvances (P24: the pay groups a payroll reader's employers have, or the groups a manager's reports are paid in now; payrollGroupId's prepared periods, newest first; partyRelationshipId's approved employee advances for a payroll reader, never an amount); payrollPayees (P27: organizations by name, a pay group's localization payee, a payroll reader's). Refuses a user without People and an unknown choice.

parameter.description: employees and departments: the employer whose employees or departments are offered

parameter.name: departmentPartyId
parameter.description: positions: the department whose seats are offered

parameter.name: payrollStructureId
parameter.description: payElections: the structure whose elective lines are offered (P23)

parameter.name: payrollGroupId
parameter.description: payPeriods: the pay group whose periods are offered (P24)

parameter.name: partyRelationshipId
parameter.description: payAdvances: the employment whose advances are offered (P24)

service.description: The palette's People records, each opening its People screen: the directory (P2), the people mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.find#Employees reaches for the user and the text, each once, as their public work identity, opening Employee360, with recordEntity and recordId; P12: the user's own leave requests whose days, leave type or state hold the text (or any for "leave"), opening LeaveRequestDetail. No rows for a user without People.

A person's record as Shared/Employee360 shows it under appRoot (design §4 Employee360's per-app context, crosscut §3.4; People.js employee360Apps): mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.get#Employee360's answer narrowed to the regions the app shows (People every admitted region; Commons the Overview and the user's own personal information; Insights the Overview, read only), the fields the user may change there and the return link. A context narrows and grants nothing. A person outside the user's People scope answers recordFound false; another app root is refused (PEOPLE_CONTEXT), and People's mount needs the People root (PEOPLE_UNAVAILABLE).

parameter.name: record
parameter.description: partyId, overview, personalInfo (when shown), partyRelationshipId, hostEmploymentId (the employment host, when its files and activity are shown), compensation (P23: People's mount, a payroll reader of the opened employment's employer: PayrollSetupServices.get#Compensation's answer; absent otherwise)

service.description: Where the user opens a person's record from an app with no Employee360 context (Projects' PersonDetail, Admin's UserDetail): People/Employees/Employee360 for a People user whose scope admits the person as staff or team, Commons/People/Employee360 for one it admits otherwise (the person themselves), else no url. The link adds no right; Employee360 checks again.

People's record-lookup provider (People.xml shell-providers, people.records; design §1.4 Comms hooks): the Person over the directory projection. search: the people find#Employees reaches for text, as optionList of {value: mantle.party.Party|id, label}; info and card: a person the user's People scope admits, as their public work identity, with their Employee360 link (a person it does not admit is left out, so another provider answers for them); P12: a leave request (mantle.humanres.leave.LeaveRequest) the user reads, as its person, days, what it charges and state (never its type or reason), opening LeaveRequestDetail; links: the people a message's Employee360 links name, up to five.

People's Today source (design §1.4 Today; People.xml and Commons.xml shell-providers, F64; get#UserTodayItems calls it): the People decisions waiting on the user (mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.find#DueWork's decision: a request whose step waiting they may decide now, PEOPLE_REQUEST_APPROVE), each opening where it is decided (PositionDetail, the person's Employee360); and P10 the user's own weeks to submit (my week not submitted: mantle.work.TimesheetServices.find#WeeksToSubmit, kind timesheet), for one who keeps time under People (a People user or a self-service employee by the time area's grant) and does not open Projects, whose own source answers them there, each opening the week in People's My time; and P12 the leave starting today or tomorrow of a manager's live reports (kind leave, PEOPLE_TEAM_VIEW: who is out, never why; not a colleague's day the team calendar shows), each opening the request; and P18 the user's own verified qualifications expiring within thirty days or expired and not renewed (kind qualification, mantle.humanres.DevelopmentServices.find#Qualifications' attention, PEOPLE_SELF_SERVICE: its type and expiry, never its number), each opening their qualifications; and P19 training due (kind training, DevelopmentServices.find#Training's due: the user's own enrolled sessions and those they train, starting within seven days), each opening the session; and P20 a review step due (kind review, mantle.humanres.ReviewServices.find#Reviews' to do, where Reviews & goals opens to the user: their own self assessment, the assessment of a person they review, feedback asked of them, with the cycle and the due day, never a rating or an answer), each opening the review. Another user's Today gets none. Declared on both roots, it is taken once.

The links of Shared/PeopleSelfService under the app that mounts it (People or Commons; design §3 SelfService): the user's own employee record (People's Employee360 for a People user who reads it, else Commons'), and for a People user People's Approvals and Home; P10: the user's own week (People's My time, when People's time area opens to them). Refuses another app root (PEOPLE_CONTEXT). Grants nothing: get#SelfService checks the user.

service.description: Who has a skill and is free over the days (SkillsMatrix's and SkillsMatrixTui's Find available): Projects' mantle.work.ResourceServices.find#StaffingCandidates (skill, dates, hours a week), bounded to the people the user's skills matrix keeps (mantle.humanres.DevelopmentServices.get#SkillsMatrix's scopePartyIds, with the same employer, unit, job class and name), ranked by free hours and skill, each as text: free hours of those needed, the skill's level (self-declared said so), the open projects the user sees and, for a holder of PAYROLL_VIEW, the cost rate (an employee's pay, Y2). Refuses a user who reads no one's skills (PERMISSION_DENIED) and what the staffing search refuses (its dates and hours).
